# Agent rules

<!-- Generated by `npm run rules:docs`. Edit scripts/lib/rules.mjs, not this file. -->

Every convention this project enforces mechanically, one section per check.
These are the same functions `npm run rules` runs, so a rule described here is a
rule that will fail your pull request, and a rule missing here is not enforced.

Run them yourself before opening a pull request:

```bash
npm run rules                     # everything checkable from the working tree
npm run rules -- --base origin/main   # adds the history-aware checks CI runs
```

## CA001 Migrations are append-only

Runs only with a base revision (`--base <ref>`); CI supplies one on every pull request.

**Checks.** No SQL file already committed under supabase/migrations/ may be modified, renamed, or deleted.

**Why.** Other contributors and every deployed instance have already run those files. Editing one silently produces divergent schemas that no migration can reconcile.

**If it fails.** Revert the edit and add a new supabase/migrations/00NN_name.sql that alters the schema forward.

## CA002 Migration filenames are numbered and ordered

**Checks.** Every migration is named 00NN_snake_case.sql, numbers are unique, and a newly added migration takes a number higher than every existing one.

**Why.** Supabase applies migrations in filename order. A duplicate or lower number reorders the schema on a fresh install but not on an existing one, so the two stop matching.

**If it fails.** Rename your file to one past the highest number currently in supabase/migrations/.

## CA003 Every table has RLS and an owner policy

**Checks.** Each table created in supabase/migrations/ is later given `enable row level security` and at least one `create policy`.

**Why.** The anon key ships inside the client bundle by design, so row level security is the only boundary. A table without it is world-readable by anyone who opens devtools.

**If it fails.** Add `alter table <name> enable row level security;` and an owner policy matching supabase/migrations/0003_rls_policies.sql.

## CA004 web/ holds no AI or service-role credentials

**Checks.** web/ may not mention SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN, GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY anywhere except the guard list in web/lib/env.ts, which must keep listing them.

**Why.** web/ is the cloud plane. A provider key placed there is deployed to Vercel and billed per token, which is the exact arrangement this project exists to avoid.

**If it fails.** Move the credential to runner/, which runs on the contributor's own machine, and read it from runner/.env there.

## CA005 web/ never calls a model

**Checks.** No file under web/ may reference a provider API host or import a provider SDK.

**Why.** The two-plane split is what keeps the app free to run: web/ queues a job row, and the local runner spends the contributor's own subscription. A direct call from web/ reintroduces metered billing.

**If it fails.** Insert a row into the jobs table and let runner/index.mjs claim it.

## CA006 README editions stay synchronized

**Checks.** README.md and README.ko.md are byte-identical, and README.en.md carries the same number of headings.

**Why.** README.ko.md exists so older links keep working; it is the same document. An English edition that lags behind sends contributors setup steps that no longer exist.

**If it fails.** Apply the change to all three editions in the same commit.

## CA008 No new dependencies without a stated reason

Reported for review; does not fail the build on its own.

Runs only with a base revision (`--base <ref>`); CI supplies one on every pull request.

**Checks.** A dependency added to any package.json is reported for human review.

**Why.** Every dependency is code that runs on a contributor's machine with their CLI subscriptions signed in. The bar is a need the standard library cannot meet, and that judgement is a person's to make.

**If it fails.** Say in the pull request why the standard library or an installed package cannot do it. If it can, remove the dependency.

## CA009 Schema changes regenerate the TypeScript types

Runs only with a base revision (`--base <ref>`); CI supplies one on every pull request.

**Checks.** If supabase/migrations/ gains a file, web/lib/supabase/database.types.ts changes too.

**Why.** The generated types are what makes a wrong column name a build error. Left stale, they describe a database that no longer exists and every check still passes.

**If it fails.** Run `supabase gen types typescript --linked > web/lib/supabase/database.types.ts` and commit the result.

## CA010 No credentials are committed

**Checks.** Tracked text files contain no API key, token, or private key matching a known provider format.

**Why.** A key pushed to a public repository is compromised the moment it lands, and rewriting history does not un-publish it.

**If it fails.** Remove the value, rotate the key at the provider, and read it from an untracked .env file instead.

## CA011 Agent context files stay wired together

**Checks.** AGENTS.md exists and states the verification commands, CLAUDE.md delegates to it, and every MCP server named in .mcp.json points at a file that exists.

**Why.** AGENTS.md is the single source so instructions cannot drift between Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Copilot. A dangling pointer means one agent silently works without the rules.

**If it fails.** Keep the guidance in AGENTS.md and leave the other files as pointers to it.

## CA012 The rule document matches the rules

**Checks.** docs/AGENT-RULES.md is exactly what `npm run rules -- --docs` produces.

**Why.** The document is generated from this file. Regenerating it in CI is what guarantees an agent reading the document is reading the checks that will actually run.

**If it fails.** Run `npm run rules:docs` and commit the result.

## CA013 Commit subjects are English and imperative

Runs only with a base revision (`--base <ref>`); CI supplies one on every pull request.

**Checks.** Each subject is ASCII, at most 72 characters, starts with a capital, has no trailing period, and uses "Add" rather than "Added" or "Adds".

**Why.** Git itself writes this way ("Merge branch..."), so the log reads as one voice. The 72-character limit is what keeps `git log --oneline` from wrapping.

**If it fails.** Rewrite the subject, for example "Add per-stage outcome tracking to the calendar".

## CA014 The Node toolchain is pinned consistently

**Checks.** All three package.json files declare the same engines.node, and .nvmrc and .node-version agree with it.

**Why.** The runner spawns CLI subprocesses and the web app builds on Vercel. When the pinned versions disagree, a contributor reproduces a bug on a Node the maintainer never runs.

**If it fails.** Set the same range in every manifest and the same major in both version files.

## CA015 Every allowed provider is fully wired

**Checks.** Each provider slug accepted by runner/safety.mjs has a runner/providers/<slug>.mjs and is imported by runner/execute.mjs.

**Why.** Adding a provider takes four edits across three files (docs/HARNESS-ENGINEERING.md section 7). Miss one and the failure only appears when a user picks that model in the prompt screen.

**If it fails.** Add the harness file, register the login check in runner/safety.mjs, and map the process in runner/execute.mjs.
